Definition: from the same as G3559; to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently:--admonish, warn.
BiblicalUsage: Noutheteo means to put someone in mind, to warn or admonish gently, face to face. Paul tells the Ephesian elders he warned every one of them night and day with tears for three years in Acts 20:31, and he is confident the Romans can admonish one another in Romans 15:14. The same word carries a father's tone in 1 Corinthians 4:14, where Paul warns the Corinthians as his beloved sons rather than shaming them, and a preacher's aim in Colossians 1:28, warning every man so that every man may stand perfect in Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe warning is part of preaching, not an extra to it, because people only change when someone loves them enough to tell them the truth. That is why I hold that tears belong with admonition: the warning that costs the speaker nothing is rarely worth hearing.
